THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 28.01.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WP(C) NO. 25363 OF 2025  3  2026:KER:6937  BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.

 W.P.(C) No.25363 of 2025  ---------------------------------
 Dated this the 28th day of January, 2026

JUDGMENT Petitioner seeks for a direction to afford police protection to the life, property and workmen of the petitioner.
2.

Petitioner claims to be a business woman indulging in sale of frozen meats, meat products, fish,
fruits and vegetables and other articles under the name and style 'St.Joseph Cold Storage' at Litty Mol John vs The Station House Officer on 28 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126571815/
2 Erattayar, Idukki.
The business is claimed to be conducted in Building No.7-816 of Erattayar Grama Panchayath in accordance with the rules and regulations.
Petitioner contends that she has obtained all the licences required under law and relies upon Ext.P1 to Ext.P3.

According to the petitioner,
respondents 3 to 5 are obstructing the conduct of business as they are competitors in the same field of business.
It is in such circumstance that the petitioner approached this Court seeking police protection after the police failed to act in accordance with law pursuant to Ext.P5 request.
3. Though notice to respondents 3 to 5 had been served, none appears on his behalf.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as WP(C) NO. 25363 OF 2025 2026:KER:6937 the learned Government Pleader.

5. On 10.07.2025, at the time of admission, this Court granted an interim order directing the first respondent to afford adequate protection to the life of the petitioner and her employees for a limited period.
Since respondents 3 to 5 have not opposed the writ petition, I am of the view that the interim order dated 10.07.2025 ought to be continued.

Accordingly, there will be a direction to the first respondent to afford adequate police protection to the life of the petitioner and her employees from any illegal acts of respondents 3 to 5 or anybody acting under them, as long as the licences are valid.
It is clarified that the protection need be afforded only when the petitioner intimates in writing about the existence of any imminent threat to her life or business.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.

Sd/-
